promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: The nature of God across religions

questions.q: What does the term 'monotheism' mean?
questions.explain: Monotheism is belief in a single God, as found in Christianity, Islam and Judaism.

questions.q: What does 'polytheism' mean?
options: Belief that God is beyond the universe
Belief that God does not exist
questions.explain: Polytheism is the belief in and worship of many gods or deities.

questions.q: The divine attribute 'omnipotent' means that God is:
questions.explain: Omnipotent describes God as having unlimited power to do anything.

questions.q: The divine attribute 'omniscient' means that God is:
questions.explain: Omniscient means God knows everything, including the past, present and future.

questions.q: The divine attribute 'omnibenevolent' means that God is:
questions.explain: Omnibenevolent describes God as perfectly loving and good towards creation.

questions.q: The divine attribute 'omnipresent' means that God is:
questions.explain: Omnipresent means God is present in all places at the same time.

questions.q: In Christianity, the belief that God is three persons in one is known as:
questions.explain: The Trinity is the Christian belief in one God as Father, Son and Holy Spirit.

questions.q: Which term describes the Islamic belief in the absolute oneness of God?
questions.explain: Tawhid is the Muslim belief in the oneness and unity of Allah.

questions.q: Which statement best describes God as 'transcendent'?
options: God is beyond and outside the universe
God is present and active within the world
questions.explain: A transcendent God exists beyond space, time and the physical universe.

questions.q: Which statement best describes God as 'immanent'?
options: God is present and active within the world
God is entirely separate from creation
God has no beginning or end
questions.explain: An immanent God is involved in and present throughout creation and human life.

questions.q: In Hinduism, Brahman is best understood as:
options: The ultimate reality present in all things
The belief that God does not exist
questions.explain: Brahman is the supreme, ultimate reality or spirit underlying all existence in Hinduism.

questions.q: To describe God as 'eternal' means that God:
options: Has no beginning and no end
Can be in only one place at a time
Depends on the universe to exist
questions.explain: An eternal God exists outside time, with no beginning and no end.

questions.q: Why does the problem of evil challenge belief in God?
options: An all-loving, all-powerful God would be expected to prevent evil and suffering
It proves that many gods must exist
It shows that God is present in the world
It demonstrates that God is all-knowing
questions.explain: The existence of evil seems to conflict with God being both omnipotent and omnibenevolent.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines 'atheism'?
options: The belief that there is no God
The view that God's existence cannot be known
The belief that God is present in all things
questions.explain: Atheism is the rejection or absence of belief in the existence of any god.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes 'agnosticism'?
options: The view that we cannot know whether God exists
The firm belief that God exists
The belief that there are many gods
The worship of one God only
questions.explain: An agnostic holds that the existence of God is unknown or unknowable.

questions.q: The design (teleological) argument for God's existence claims that:
options: The order and complexity of the universe suggests a designer
Everything that begins to exist must have a cause
Evil in the world disproves God
questions.explain: The design argument reasons that the apparent order and purpose in nature points to God as a designer.

questions.q: What is the difference between a 'personal' and an 'impersonal' idea of God?
options: A personal God can be related to like a being, while an impersonal God is more like a force or principle
A personal God has many forms, while an impersonal God has one
A personal God is all-powerful, while an impersonal God is not
A personal God does not exist, while an impersonal God does
questions.explain: A personal God is one people can have a relationship with, whereas an impersonal God is an abstract force or reality.

questions.q: The First Cause (cosmological) argument suggests that God is needed as:
options: The uncaused cause of the universe's existence
questions.explain: The cosmological argument reasons that the universe must have a first, uncaused cause, which is God.

questions.q: A believer says, 'God already knows every choice I will make tomorrow.' Which attribute is being described?
questions.explain: Knowing all future choices reflects God being all-knowing, or omniscient.

questions.q: Someone says, 'The suffering of innocent children is why I cannot believe in a loving God.' Which response to belief are they using?
questions.explain: Pointing to undeserved suffering as a reason to doubt God is an example of the problem of evil.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Religious Studies (4RS1) specification; Beliefs about Deity
